about: Homework for this pillar, one list per AI (Claude writes it; tools/kit/render.py in jpavia10/prometheus-hub turns it into docs/agents/QUEUE_{ai}.md and the Drive docs). Every task says exactly what to read, what to make, how many, where to save it, how Claude checks it and what makes it not done. A task is done only when the file passes the checks, never because it was sent.

tasks.title: Aegis: California homeowners insurance as the Department of Insurance explains it (coverages A to F, replacement cost, extended replacement, the FAIR Plan, the home inventory, claim deadlines)
tasks.why: Aegis checks the house's contents against the personal-property limit. Joseph should also see, from the regulator, what each coverage letter means, what replacement cost versus actual cash value changes, and how long an insurer has to answer a claim.
tasks.unlocks: Aegis's cover panel explains each limit it reads and the claim timeline in the Claims section.
inputs: https://www.insurance.ca.gov (the residential insurance consumer pages and guides)
California Code of Regulations, title 10, sections 2695.5 and 2695.7 (Fair Claims Settlement Practices)
steps: One row per point: each coverage A to F (what it pays for); replacement cost and actual cash value; extended replacement cost; what the FAIR Plan is and what it does not cover; what CDI says to put in a home inventory; the claim deadlines (acknowledge, accept or deny, pay) with the regulation section.

deliver.shape: JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below

fields.name: topic
fields.rule: coverage, valuation, FAIR Plan, inventory or claims

fields.name: point
fields.rule: one plain sentence

fields.name: quote
fields.rule: the words on the page that say it, copied exactly

fields.name: source_url
fields.rule: the official page that shows the value (a .gov, the statute, or the agency's own page)

fields.name: checked
fields.rule: the day you read it, YYYY-MM-DD

tasks.done_when: At least 18 rows covering all five topics.
checks: Claude opens ten source URLs at random and finds each quote on the page.
rejected_if: a value without a source URL that shows it
rows missing to reach the count
a source that is a blog, forum, law-firm marketing page or AI summary where an official page exists
a value for a year that has not been published yet presented as if it had (write "not published as of {date}" instead)
a quote that is not on the page word for word

tasks.title: Aegis: California auto insurance requirements in force for 2026 (the minimum limits after SB 1107, proof of insurance, the good driver discount)
tasks.why: Aegis keeps the auto policy's liability limit; it should say when that limit is below the state minimum, and the minimums changed on January 1, 2025.
tasks.unlocks: Aegis flags an auto policy below California's minimum and shows the minimum beside the limit.
steps: Rows: bodily injury per person, per accident, property damage (the minimums in force in 2026, with the date they took effect and what they were before); the proof of insurance rules; uninsured motorist coverage (offered, may be waived in writing?); the good driver discount (who qualifies, how much).

tasks.title: Aegis: what California and federal law say about warranties and service contracts (Song-Beverly, Magnuson-Moss), with the section for each
tasks.why: Aegis lists the warranties Hearth and Records hold. Joseph should know what the law adds on top: implied warranties and how long they last, what a written warranty must state, and the rules for extended warranties (service contracts).
tasks.unlocks: Aegis's warranty list explains what is still covered after a written warranty ends, and when a service contract can be cancelled.
inputs: California Civil Code sections 1790 to 1795.8 (Song-Beverly Consumer Warranty Act) on https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov
15 U.S.C. 2301 to 2312 and the FTC's guide https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/businesspersons-guide-federal-warranty-law
steps: Rows: the implied warranty of merchantability and of fitness (what each is, how long it lasts in California, 1791.1); full versus limited written warranties (Magnuson-Moss); what a written warranty must disclose; service contracts in California (who must be licensed, cancellation and refund rules, 1794.4 and 1794.41); repair time and the number of attempts before a replacement or refund (1793.2).

deliver.shape: JSON array, one object per row, exactly the fields below

fields.name: law
fields.rule: Song-Beverly or Magnuson-Moss

fields.name: point
fields.rule: one plain sentence

fields.name: section
fields.rule: the section number

fields.name: quote
fields.rule: the words of the section, copied exactly

fields.name: source_url
fields.rule: the official page that shows the value (a .gov, the statute, or the agency's own page)

fields.name: checked
fields.rule: the day you read it, YYYY-MM-DD

checks: Claude opens every source URL and finds each quote.

tasks.title: Aegis: the California FAIR Plan, what it covers and what it leaves out
tasks.why: Frazier Park is a high fire-risk area; many homes there end up on the FAIR Plan. Aegis checks Hearth's contents against the policy limit and needs the FAIR Plan's own limits and gaps.
tasks.unlocks: Aegis can say what a FAIR Plan policy leaves uncovered and what a difference-in-conditions policy adds.
steps: From the FAIR Plan's and the Department of Insurance's own pages: the dwelling and contents limits, the perils covered, what is excluded (liability, water, theft and others), and how a difference-in-conditions policy fills the gap.

tasks.title: Aegis: second reader on Gemini's California homeowners insurance facts
tasks.why: Nothing Gemini delivers is built on until a second reader has checked it.
tasks.unlocks: Claude builds from the file only after this check.
inputs: Gemini's file aegis_gemini_ca-homeowners_*.json in the folder below (AEG-GEM-01)
steps: Open Gemini's file. Pick 12 rows at random (every row if fewer).
For each, open its source URL and compare every field with the page: agree, or what the page says instead.
Add up to 5 rows Gemini missed, in Gemini's exact shape.

deliver.shape: markdown table: row | Gemini says | what I found | URL | agree/differ, then the list of what is missing

fields.name: agree/differ
fields.rule: differ needs what you found and where

checks: Claude re-reads three of your 'differ' rows against the page.
rejected_if: a verdict without the page it came from
